correctness.rationale: For every a,b>=2, the one-body spectrum is +sqrt(ab), -sqrt(ab), and zero (multiplicity a+b-2). Any boson eigenvector at nonzero two-body energy has some nonzero diagonal collision amplitude; hence nondecaying states are necessarily zero modes. An exact block calculation on symmetric amplitude matrices gives cross-block double centering, within-part unsigned incidence kernels, and one normalized mixed vector. Their mutually orthogonal projectors sum to the claimed projector and yield dimension ((a+b-1)(a+b-4))/2+[a=2]+[b=2]. Positive diagonal loss rates make every other spectral mode strictly decaying; exact rational projectors and an independent collision-observability Krylov rank computation agree for stated finite cases. No finite test is extrapolated to prove all sizes.

value.rationale: The exact response of natural biclique networks to two-boson local collision loss has a motivated physical use: determining protected subspaces and detection from arbitrary input without time integration. The complete projector and localized capture law reveal a sharp one-unit dark-space anomaly when either part has size two; K_{2,4} and K_{3,3} have equal vertex count but different protected ranks and capture. The result is an infinite-size structural classification, not an arbitrary finite slice or recomputed star/cycle case.
